title: Pan-Cooked Chicken Breast for Pasta
description: Juicy, golden chicken breast seasoned with salt and pepper, pan-seared in a little olive oil, and sliced for pasta dishes or salads.

steps.text: If the chicken breast is very thick, cut it horizontally into two thinner pieces so it cooks evenly.
Sprinkle both sides with salt and black pepper. Add a little paprika or garlic powder if desired.

Heat 5 g olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken about 4–5 minutes on each side, reducing the heat if it browns too fast. Cooking time varies with thickness; check that the thickest part reaches 74°C.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain. Use the same pan and its browned juices when making the pasta sauce.

notes: This makes approximately 150 g cooked chicken from 200 g raw chicken breast. The exact cooked yield depends on moisture lost during cooking.
A food thermometer is the best way to ensure the thickest part reaches 74°C; do not rely on color alone.
Macros assume all 5 g of olive oil is retained in the finished serving. Optional seasoning and salt contribute negligible calories.
Nutrition uses standard estimates for raw, skinless chicken breast (120 kcal, 22.5 g protein, 2.6 g fat per 100 g) and olive oil.
